diagrams.title: L0 · System context
diagrams.description: System context: the machine manager is one box. The control plane and humans + mmctl call it; it drives the bare-metal providers, boots and audits the machines, which pull their boot image from S3, and it alerts in Slack. Nothing inside is shown yet, so L1 opens it.

diagrams.title: L1 · The machine manager
diagrams.description: L0's box opened one level: its boundary services — private gRPC, webapi, provider registry, cluster reconcile, SSH + BMC ops and the boot server — sit in the Machine manager box, while the control plane, humans, providers and machines stay outside it.

diagrams.title: L1b · The machine side
diagrams.description: The fleet end of the same system. Bare-metal machines run the machine-agent, which registers and heartbeats into public gRPC inside the manager's box; the River queue uploads diagnostics to S3 and webapi confirms actions in Slack, both outside. The fleet drives these outward relations.

diagrams.title: L2 · Inside — queue and dispatch
diagrams.description: Inside the box, first slice: requests land on the River queue, which dispatches provision jobs to the provider registry, audit work to SSH + BMC ops and diagnostic events to the janitor; the janitor proposes actions back to webapi. L2b carries the state writes this slice leaves out.

diagrams.title: L2b · Inside — the state writes
diagrams.description: Inside the box, second slice: the writes into the Postgres state store — job rows from the queue, machine rows from private gRPC, machine state from public gRPC heartbeats and cluster state from the reconcile loop. Same box, same manager; only the state edges are drawn here.
